title: When Tulips Bankrupted Ottoman Nobles
hook: During the 1720s, rare tulip bulbs cost more than palace mansions.

scenes.text: In the 1720s, during the reign of Sultan Ahmed III, Istanbul succumbed to an extravagant obsession known as the 'Tulip Era'.

scenes.text: The prized flower was the slender Ottoman tulip, bred for razor-sharp dagger petals and intricate variegated color flame patterns.

scenes.text: Prices exploded: a single rare bulb called 'Light of the Mind' sold for over one thousand gold coins, bankrupting aristocratic viziers.

scenes.text: At lavish nocturnal palace garden festivals, live tortoises with small candles strapped to their shells wandered among flowerbeds.
